title: Custody, Safeguarding and Client Assets
summary: Why custody is the critical risk in digital assets, how client assets are held and protected, and what assurance the board needs that client holdings are safe and reconciled.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Why custody is the critical risk in digital assets, how client assets are held and protected, and what assurance the board needs that client holdings are safe and reconciled.
Learning Objectives: Explain how private keys, wallets and custody arrangements protect or expose client assets
Evaluate segregation, reconciliation and safeguarding controls
Judge the adequacy of independent assurance over client holdings
Syllabus: Hot, warm and cold storage, multi-signature and key management
Segregation of client assets and treatment on insolvency
Reconciliation, proof of reserves and their limits
Sub-custody and third-party custodian due diligence
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors of firms offering, or planning to offer, digital asset products and services
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for digital asset strategy, risk, compliance and operations
Board committee members and company secretaries supporting oversight of new business lines
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No technical background in blockchain or digital assets is required.
Core Reading: FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-Asset Activities and Markets (2023)
IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (2023)
Basel Committee, Prudential Treatment of Cryptoasset Exposures (2022)
